contract: Anthropic Message Batches provider of integration/ai-batch on the pinned Req: anthropic-version 2026-10-21, one request per operation with the injected key as x-api-key, retry and redirect off, bounded response bodies; each item's params are the synchronous ai-text-anthropic body (translate, req_llm prepare_request/4 and encode_body/1 with a placeholder key) minus stream false; the outer anthropic-beta is the sorted union of allowed item values, anything else refused; create, retrieve, cancel and streamed results decoded from the documented formats (in_progress running, canceling ending, ended with counts; succeeded, errored, canceled, expired lines joined by custom_id); orphans always empty; documented statuses mapped by the synchronous provider's table; caps 100,000 requests and 256,000,000 create-body bytes.
limits: Stub evidence only (R5): conformance to the pinned documented format, never current live behaviour, turnaround, the batch discount, billing of result types, retention or rate limits.

Create requests are validated against a schema hand-derived from named sections of Anthropic's documentation fetched 2026-11-09; no official machine-readable specification was found; conformance beyond the documented examples is not claimed.

Upstream risk: the encoded item body is read from the request's :json option after req_llm's documented encode_body/1 callback, an undocumented location; the root mix.exs declares req_llm ~> 1.30 locked at 1.30.0, so a lock update could move it, and the drift test over a fixed corpus is the guard.
Body equivalence with the synchronous call is shown over a finite corpus only; a beta value enabled by one item is sent for the whole batch (allowed values only).
The results endpoint has no paging: each page re-reads the stream from the start under the scan bound.
Every consumer must merge config :req_llm, load_dotenv: false by hand (README, Install configuration); the Piece test asserts only that the README carries the exact line.

grounding.claim: Every captured create request is validated with jsv against this schema hand-derived from Anthropic's 'Create a Message Batch' and 'Batch processing' (fetched 2026-11-09) and the ELZ-079 Messages request members, plus method, path, outer anthropic-version and exact anthropic-beta union, the injected key, unique custom_id, max_tokens above zero and absent stream, speed, fallbacks and sampling fields. Not an official specification.

Listed scenarios against in-process function-plug stubs in Anthropic's documented formats, run through the interface conformance kit: submit accepted, lost (unknown, second dispatch refused) and 400, 401, 413, 429 with retry-after, 529, 500 and malformed 2xx mapped with one request each and orphans empty; outer beta union and refusal of other betas; drift of item params and headers against the pinned req_llm 1.30.0 snapshot; item params equal to the synchronous body minus stream false over the fixed corpus; create-body bound at and one under its size; status sequence in_progress, canceling, ended and 401, 404, 429, 529 and malformed batches; cancel acknowledged, lost and 404; streamed results in chunks with mixed result types out of order, absent usage fields, errored types, malformed messages, unknown and duplicate custom_id, missing item, contiguous pages, deep cursor scan limit, line limit and malformed line; redaction with ambient keys set; README Install configuration line; source audit. Finite scenarios, no live call, not proofs.
Req 0.7.5 request options (retry, redirect, decode_body, compressed, into with halt) and the :plug test transport.

req_llm 1.30.0 (Hex checksum 1c4b19608aa982de5ea396cc6de3d3738e72480182ba11c184e028a4af305edb) documented provider callbacks prepare_request/4 and encode_body/1 for Anthropic body encoding; the :json location of the encoded body is an observation of the pinned version guarded by the drift test.

Anthropic's live Message Batches API behaves as documented; errored, canceled and expired requests are not billed (documented only); the allowed beta values are harmless for items that do not use the feature; a 429 or 529 meaning 'before generation' authorizes nothing; the host keeps the key Need truthful.

telemetry.contract: No Elzoo event; req_llm is used only to build item bodies and sends nothing, Req emits no events of its own. Own events through runtime/telemetry: future task.

config.contract: Construction-time provider term (optional HTTPS base URL; a test plug), fixed API version 2026-10-21, retry and redirect off, receive timeout and bounds from the interface Config, key from the injected Need; no hot reconfiguration.

control.contract: Call-scoped; dispatch, rearm and expiry of submit and cancel are the delivery/effect-intent owner's Control; cancel is a request to Anthropic, not a local drain.
